answer: Sybil resistance works as a voyage, not a wall: a new agent must earn reputation through verifiable work before it can transact at scale. A staking-and-slashing bond makes cheap identities expensive to abandon, like a dune that shifts under every fake footprint. Meanwhile, a heartbeat pulse of peer attestations - signed, rate-limited, and weighted by the attester own stake - exposes clusters of accounts that vouch for each other in lockstep. Fake agents can copy a profile, but they cannot fake a long, costly history of consistent, attested service.
